payload.stories:
SECOND FILL. The first named eight "props" lifted from the pitch's feature list; the frame records TWO props with needs N1-N12, and every story below realizes a prop and names the needs it serves.

PROP 1 — THE AGENT WALKING THE LOOP (needs N1 read any source · N2 find without four attempts, with context · N3 know the rules that bind this step · N4 edit many sites at once · N5 search what shipped).
PROP 2 — THE OWNER WHO OWNS AN ITERATION THEY DID NOT WATCH (needs N6 mechanical checks are mechanical · N7 a lint never parks an unattended run · N8 the record survives carelessness · N9 the audit distinguishes computed from asserted · N10 a gate is reviewed not just filled · N11 a reopen verdict does something · N12 the red-team round is adversarial).

Evidence sides are deliberately EMPTY — they fill at validation.

=====================================================================
S1 — THE GATE THAT REVIEWS ITSELF   [KILLER]   PROP 2 · N10, N11, N12
=====================================================================
1 SETUP. An agent reaches a gate at the end of a milestone. It has built the thing, its tests are green, it wants to move on. The owner is asleep.
2 THE ASK. The form shows the gate's own acceptance items — and four more it cannot leave blank: verify, validate, red-team, verdict. It did not choose to run them; nothing asked whether it would like to.
3 THE TURN. In the validate round it reads the work against the REQUIREMENT REGISTER rather than against its own plan, and finds a requirement its own design violates.
4 THE RED TEAM. It argues the case FOR passing anyway, as strongly as it can, then names the kill-criterion — what would have to be true for reopening to be wrong — and goes looking. It is not met.
5 THE VERDICT. REOPEN. The named states and their downstream cone come back to life; the earlier fills are marked superseded, not erased.
6 THE MORNING. The owner reads a gate that caught its own author — a green tick with the case against it underneath, and a record of what did not survive.
WHY KILLER: this is the iteration. If a gate can still pass without its rounds, nothing else here matters. The proof standard is high because this exact scenario failed once already: the rounds were required in writing, and every gate in the project's history passed without them.

=====================================================================
S2 — THE AGENT WHO STOPS WRITING SCRIPTS   [KILLER]   PROP 1 · N1, N2, N4, N5
=====================================================================
1 SETUP. The agent needs to know how the predecessor system solved a problem it is about to re-solve. The answer is in a file that is not in this worktree, in a revision that shipped weeks ago.
2 THE OLD WAY. It writes a script — not from preference, but because the read lane cannot reach outside the iteration's root and the search lane cannot see a revision. The owner sees the script go by and asks why the tools it built are not being used.
3 THE NEW WAY (N1, N5). One search, scoped to a revision. The predecessor's checklist and every shipped iteration's evidence are as reachable as today's files, without checking anything out.
4 THE CONTEXT (N2). Matches come back WITH the lines around them, in the same answer, so the agent reads the answer instead of reading a line number and going back for a second call.
5 THE EDIT (N4). The fix touches ten places across five files. One batch call, atomic by construction: every edit verified before any is written, so a bad match on the tenth means the first nine never happened.
6 THE OUTCOME. No script. Nothing to declare, nothing to log, nothing to fix at the next retro.
WHY KILLER: the lane is judged by whether the honest path runs inside it. Six times in one day it did not, and each cost an owner's evening.

=====================================================================
S3 — THE SECOND AGENT   [KILLER]   PROP 1 · no numbered need
=====================================================================
1 SETUP. Two agents, two iterations, at once. One is improving the engine.
2 THE TRAP. If each ran the engine from its own worktree the two iterations would be judged by DIFFERENT machines — one collecting the review rounds, one not. A gate would stop meaning one thing.
3 THE STEP. The engine change is promoted: trunk pulled current first, engine files only, the whole suite run IN TRUNK after the copy and before the commit, and on any failure trunk restored exactly.
4 THE TURN. The suite comes back red. Nothing is committed; the other agent never sees a broken judge. The refusal NAMES the failing test, so the fix takes a minute rather than an hour.
5 THE OUTCOME. Both agents run against one judge, and the one building the engine gets its own improvement in the same session.
WHY KILLER: the goal is iterations that run alone and in parallel. Per-worktree engines, waiting for the close, and asking the owner all break exactly when the second agent appears.
REGISTER NOTE: realizes PROP 1 but no numbered need — it comes from an owner ruling issued after the frame was written. Sourced at M3 to the ruling and this story.

=====================================================================
S4 — THE WRONG ARGUMENT   PROP 1 · no numbered need
=====================================================================
1 SETUP. The agent mistypes an argument name.
2 THE OLD WAY. The value arrives as undefined, the tool coerces it into something plausible, and the answer comes back confident and wrong. The agent proceeds on it. Nothing anywhere is red.
3 THE NEW WAY. Dispatch refuses before doing any work: the clause, what was expected, what arrived, and the remedy with the argument names spelled out.
4 THE FINE DISTINCTION. An argument that is ABSENT is not one explicitly passed as empty. The first is a mistake, the second a deliberate statement. The guard learned this the hard way — its first version refused a legitimate empty value and became the very workaround pressure it was built to remove.
REGISTER NOTE: as S3 — owner ruling, no numbered need, sourced at M3.

=====================================================================
S5 — THE CHECK THAT DOES NOT PRETEND   PROP 2 · N6, N7
=====================================================================
1 SETUP. A gate asks whether the work adheres to the models, and whether every requirement has a verification method.
2 THE HONEST ANSWER. It cannot be computed today — requirements are prose, not nodes, so nothing mechanical can join them to anything.
3 THE TURN (N7). The lint returns DEFER with the reason, rather than PASS. A deferral is visible; a false pass is not. And it decides or defers — there is no third outcome that leaves an unattended run parked.
4 THE OUTCOME. The deferral carries a risk entry naming what would have to change — items as nodes — which is an owner's decision and its own iteration.
5 THE RULE (N6). Everything that CAN be checked mechanically is not left to the agent's judgement, because an agent judging its own work is the failure this iteration exists to fix.

=====================================================================
S6 — THE READER SIX MONTHS OUT   PROP 2 · N11
=====================================================================
1 SETUP. Someone opens this record long after it shipped and finds a state filled twice.
2 THE ASK. Which one is true, and why did the first stop being true?
3 THE ANSWER. The first fill is there, marked superseded. Between the two sits a reopened marker carrying the reason in the words of whoever ordered it.
4 THE OUTCOME. The record shows a mind being changed, which is the only kind of record worth keeping. Nothing was deleted to make the current state look clean.
5 THE PROOF THAT IT IS NOT DECORATIVE. The superseded fill is not merely present — it is USED. This iteration's own gate had to reopen the first-pass frame to recover the need register it was judging against.

=====================================================================
S7 — THE OWNER READING CHAT   PROP 2 · no numbered need
=====================================================================
1 SETUP. The owner is away. Their entire view of the run is chat and the board.
2 THE PROBLEM. The message says a requirement is satisfied and names it R3. The owner has never seen R3. The sentence reads as precision and carries nothing.
3 THE TURN. Every identifier is expanded in the message that uses it, and where the plain phrase will do, the identifier does not appear at all.
4 THE OUTCOME. The owner can adjudicate from what they were sent, which is the only thing they have.
REGISTER NOTE: as S3 and S4 — owner ruling, no numbered need, sourced at M3.

=====================================================================
S8 — THE LAW MINTED THIS AFTERNOON   [KILLER]   PROP 1 · N3
=====================================================================
1 SETUP. Four laws are minted during a single afternoon: guards are whitelists, requirements are never weakened, responsibility never delegates, a workaround must record the gap it worked around.
2 THE PROBLEM. The agent that will next violate one of them has never read it. It was trained before the law existed and it has no reason to go looking — a law it must discover is a law that binds nobody.
3 THE TURN. The agent reaches a state where one of them applies. The packet it is handed CARRIES the law, resolved and quoted, alongside the step's own guidance. It did not search; nothing asked it to remember.
4 THE EXTENSION. A law that names no state it applies to reaches nobody, and that is itself reportable — an unattached rule shows up as unattached rather than sitting quietly in the ledger looking authoritative.
5 THE OUTCOME. The rule arrives at the moment it binds, in the hands of the agent it binds.
WHY KILLER: this is the same defect as S1, at a different level. The review rounds were written and never collected; the guidance is written and never delivered. If the packet still does not carry the rules, this iteration fixed one instance of the shape and left the shape.

=====================================================================
S9 — THE TAG THAT WAS DELETED   PROP 2 · N8
=====================================================================
1 SETUP. An iteration shipped weeks ago. Its record — evidence, gates, grants — lives in the history rather than in the working tree.
2 THE CARELESSNESS. Someone deletes the local tags to tidy up. Or pushes without carrying them, which is the default behaviour and takes no mistake at all. The readable name is gone.
3 THE ASK. Six months later the owner needs what that iteration decided and why.
4 THE TURN. The evidence is still reachable — by hash from the trunk history, without the tag, without the branch, without anyone having been careful.
5 THE OUTCOME. The record's survival does not depend on anybody remembering a flag.
WHY IT MATTERS: this is the need that fails silently. Nothing goes red when a record becomes unreachable; it is discovered only when someone needs it, which is exactly when it is too late.

=====================================================================
S10 — WHO ACTUALLY CHECKED THIS   PROP 2 · N9
=====================================================================
1 SETUP. The owner opens a killer gate that an agent blessed while they were asleep. Eight checks are recorded as satisfied.
2 THE ASK. Which of those did a MACHINE decide, and which are the agent's own word?
3 THE OLD WAY. Every check reads the same — a confident sentence — and telling them apart means reading all eight closely and inferring. The distinction that matters most is the one the record does not make.
4 THE TURN. Each check carries its origin: computed, with the verdict and the fact behind it, or asserted, in the agent's words. The owner sees which is which WITHOUT reading the prose.
5 THE OUTCOME. Trust is spent where it is actually needed. The owner reads the agent's judgement carefully and lets the computed half stand — which is the whole point of computing it.
CONNECTION: S5 shows the lint DECIDING; this shows the owner READING the difference. They are two halves and the first fill only had one.
